verifications.claim: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster occurred on January 28, 1986.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the exact date of the disaster.

verifications.claim: The Challenger orbiter broke apart 73 seconds into its 25th flight (STS-51L).
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: '73 seconds after takeoff'; R3: '73 seconds after liftoff'; R4: '73 seconds after liftoff... its 10th mission'; R5: '73 seconds... 10th flight for the orbiter and the 25th flight of the Space Shuttle fleet'; R6: '25th in the program and the 10th for space shuttle Challenger'
verifications.reasoning: 73 seconds and STS-51L supported, but 'its 25th flight' incorrectly attributes program total (25th Shuttle flight) to Challenger orbiter specifically (its 10th flight).

verifications.claim: The Challenger orbiter broke apart at approximately 46,000 feet.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'at an altitude of 14,000 metres (46,000 feet)'; R5: 'about 46,000 feet (14 km)'
verifications.reasoning: References directly state the exact altitude.

verifications.claim: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster killed all seven crew members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crew of seven aboard'; R2: 'killing all seven crew members'; R3: 'claimed the lives of seven astronauts'; R4: 'killing all seven crewmembers'; R5: 'killing all seven crew members'; R6: 'seven-member crew'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant references confirm seven crew members killed.

verifications.claim: The failure was caused by O-ring seals in the right solid rocket booster failing due to cold weather.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'faulty O-rings in the shuttle's booster rockets... cold weather'; R2: 'failure of the primary and secondary O-ring seals in one of the rocket boosters... record-low temperatures'; R3: 'two rubber O-rings... right-hand solid rocket booster... severe cold'; R4: 'O-ring... solid rocket boosters... cold weather'; R5: 'O-ring seal failure in right SRB due to cold weather'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references specify O-ring failure in right SRB due to cold weather.

verifications.claim: The failure resulted in a catastrophic explosion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'catastrophic event... exploded'; R3: 'disappeared in an explosion'; R4: 'Challenger broke up'; R5: 'broke apart... fireball'
verifications.reasoning: References describe the event as an explosion or catastrophic breakup/fireball, aligning directly with the claim.

verifications.claim: This video shows the launch and the immediate aftermath of the Challenger disaster.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Video: Space Shuttle Challenger Explodes After Launch On Jan. 28, 1986... Just 73 seconds after takeoff, the shuttle broke apart'
verifications.reasoning: R2 is explicitly a video description of the launch and explosion/breakup.
